page: Microsoft Azure E96-48ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by a dedicated 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor. Built on an x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization, the configuration provides 48 virtual CPUs across 24 physical cores with two threads per core. The instance is provisioned with 672 GB of system memory, resulting in an elevated 14 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware resources also bundle 3865 GB of fast local SSD storage, while discrete GPU acceleration is not present.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong memory subsystem performance, highlighted by uncached large-block read bandwidth of 261.74 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 130.97 GB/sec. Synthetic testing confirms this strength with a PassMark memory score of 2902.5 and database operation results reaching 23765.97. Cryptographic performance is equally strong at 43847.48 due to hardware acceleration flags including AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. General-purpose compute scores reside in the average range, indicated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 15646.0 and a single-core score of 1708.0.

The constrained-core layout of this instance provides the total memory and local storage footprint of a 96-vCPU chassis while exposing only 48 active vCPUs. This configuration delivers clear qualitative cost efficiency for workloads governed by per-core software licensing, such as enterprise relational database engines. A key tradeoff lies in processing unaccelerated AI workloads; without specialized GPU hardware, large language model generation drops significantly, delivering 2.41 tokens per second on a 70B parameter model.

The technical profile aligns with demanding, memory-intensive enterprise applications. Primary suitable workloads include production relational database management systems, in-memory key-value stores, distributed data caching, and static web serving with heavy localized caching requirements.
